title: 1.2.15 Greeting with Backticks
description: Build a greeting with a template literal, then prove single quotes cannot do the same job. Auto-graded.

steps.title: Declare myName
steps.instructions: Declare a variable called `myName` and set it to your name in quotes.

steps.title: Greet with a template literal
steps.instructions: Log a greeting using backticks, embedding myName with ${...}.

steps.title: Embed a calculation too
steps.instructions: In the same greeting or a second one, embed a calculation such as ${2024 + 1}.

steps.title: Now try it with single quotes
steps.instructions: Log the same text again using single quotes instead of backticks, keeping the ${myName} part inside the single quotes. Read both outputs and note the difference.

aiCheck.prompt: The student wrote JavaScript for the lab "1.2.15 Greeting with Backticks". The task they were given: Declare a variable called `myName` and set it to your name in quotes. You cannot run their code: read it and judge what it WOULD do. Judge each criterion by whether the idea is achieved, however the student wrote it. Different variable and function names, template strings, arrow functions, semicolons, spacing, quotes and order are all fine. Do not require any particular structure unless the criterion names one. Mark a criterion missing only when the idea is absent or the code does the opposite. Code inside a comment never runs. Write each note for THIS student's own code: in a not-met note, name the exact line or name in their code that causes the problem (quote at most a few words of it), say in plain words what it does now versus what the criterion needs, and give one concrete next thing to try, but do NOT write the corrected code. In a met note, say in one short phrase what in their code satisfied it. Do not use generic praise.
